alignments.note: Finite verb with its English subject pronoun; rule 9 puts the head on the lexical verb *wilt*, which is what glosses θέλω here.

Subjunctive with supplied subject and modal auxiliary, headed on the lexical verb *do* under rule 9. The supplied complementizer *that* is folded in under rules 40 and 85 as the word introducing this verb's English clause: the deliberative subjunctive is the subordinated verbal itself, so a source token carries the subordination. Marking *that* `added` under rule 86 remains defensible, since no Greek conjunction stands here; rule 86 is scoped to a finite indicative, which this is not.
Dative pronoun with its case preposition riding along under rule 21, headed on the pronoun.
Substantival article supplying the pronoun *he*; rule 22, no participle following.
Anarthrous vocative to *Lord*; no article competes.
ἵνα realized by the complementizer *that* introducing its English clause under rule 40.

One Greek verb rendered by the support-verb phrase *receive … sight*; rules 17 and 91 head it on the meaning-bearing complement *sight*, which glosses the -βλεπ- root, while *receive* is the empty support verb. Supplied subject, modal and possessive ride along as rule 7 and 9 helpers, the possessive not `added` under rule 11. A head on *receive* is the competing reading and is refused for the same reason *bear witness* heads on *witness*.

review_notes: Every s001–s010 and t001–t019 id is partitioned exactly once.
The only genuinely contested unit is the supplied *that* at t004: folded onto ποιήσω rather than marked `added`, on the ground that the deliberative subjunctive is itself the subordinated verbal.
ἀναβλέψω's ἀνα- preverb has no separate English particle here, so rule 106 does not split anything off; the whole phrase stays one unit.
